clue.text: When cable is in place, drive forward

indicators.note: the cable is said to sit in the place, so one word is set inside the other

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: Instructions for an engineer: once the cable is fixed, move the machine forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel something is to push or drive it onwards.

clue.text: A half-hearted killer, more than ready to be drunk

definitions.text: more than ready to be drunk

indicators.note: losing half of its heart: one of the two central letters of the killer's name goes

parts.note: Jack the Ripper, the Victorian murderer, gives the word ripper for a killer

explanation.surface: A murderer with little conviction, keen to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two Ps at the centre of RIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine or fruit past mere readiness is further matured, more fully developed for drinking.

clue.text: Too soon to repeat rum distribution

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things about, so the letters of the two words are dealt out anew

explanation.surface: It is too early to hand out another round of rum, perhaps on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges REPEAT and RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something premature happens before its proper time, too early.

clue.text: Young fellow's fabrication about a theologian

indicators.note: the fabrication goes round, or about, the other pieces

parts.note: a fabrication is a lie
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A boy's tall story about a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'about' wraps the fabrication round the other pieces. The answer is a Scottish word for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A laddie is a lad or boy, especially in Scottish speech.

clue.text: Leader of union forcing a rebellion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: prising means forcing open with leverage

explanation.surface: A trade-union boss stirring up a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' takes the U of union.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a revolt against authority.

clue.text: Not expressing praise for new penal community? About right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, or about, the letter for right
a new version of the words penal community is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fresh community of convicts is unflattering, and about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal; 'About' then wraps the shuffled letters round the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that are uncomplimentary give no flattery and offer criticism instead.

clue.text: One left Rio with vessels carrying oriental fruit

indicators.note: the one is left out, taken away from the city name

parts.note: Rio, the Brazilian city, taken as written
I, the Roman numeral, stands for one

indicators.note: the vessels carry, or hold, the next piece inside them

parts.note: ships are vessels
E for east, the orient

explanation.surface: Someone sailed from Rio de Janeiro on ships laden with exotic Eastern produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes the one out of Rio; 'carrying' puts the oriental letter in the vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosehips are the red seed pods a rose forms after flowering, a fruit used for syrup.

clue.text: She tempted soldiers into wrongdoing

indicators.note: the soldiers go into the wrongdoing, inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A woman lured the troops into misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' sends the soldiers inside the wrongdoing. The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors with song.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, after the singers of myth who lured sailors to their doom.

clue.text: Relating to the figures in Book Four?

definitions.text: Relating to the figures in Book Four?

parts.words: Relating to the figures in Book Four?
parts.note: the fourth book of the Bible is named after the census counts it records, so its adjective also means to do with digits

explanation.walkthrough: Book Four is the fourth book of the Old Testament, named for its census figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything concerning digits or counting, and puns on the biblical book's title.

clue.text: Tips about parking conclude the extra reading matter

indicators.note: the tips go round, about, the other pieces

parts.note: apices, plural of apex, are tips
P is the sign for parking
to end is to conclude

explanation.surface: Advice on parking rounds off the supplementary material in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts parking and conclude inside the tips; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are supplementary sections added at the end of a book.

clue.text: It's inclined to make a racket

explanation.surface: Something sloping that kicks up a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slope joining two levels; to ramp is also to storm about noisily, rampaging.

clue.text: Tortuous roamings of a living creature

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so the letters of the word are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: The winding wanderings of some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortuous' rearranges ROAMINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism is any individual living thing, plant or animal.

clue.text: Not a country in need of food

indicators.note: not a means the letter A is taken away, left out of the country

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A land with too little to eat, or not quite a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes the A from HUNGARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hungry is starving and wants something to eat.

clue.text: Beginnings of journeys everyone hates, under a reckless driver

indicators.note: the beginnings of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A careless motorist whose trips everyone loathes being stuck behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginnings of' takes the opening letters of four words. Jehu, a king in the Bible, drove furiously, so the name means a fast driver.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Jehu drove his chariot furiously, so the name became a jocular word for a fast, wild driver.

clue.text: Just a quarter leave island subject to 5 ac

parts.note: E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass
to quit is to leave

indicators.note: 5 across is uprising: in a down clue the island goes upwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A fair arrangement: a quarter of the people leave an island in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to 5 ac' sends ELBA up the grid, giving ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial.

clue.text: Application of punishment after backchat?

indicators.note: the punishment comes after the backchat in the answer

parts.note: lip is cheeky backchat
getting stick means being punished or criticised

explanation.surface: Asking whether a caning is administered after cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' suggests applying a punishment; the answer is something applied to the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is cosmetic colour put on, or applied to, the mouth.

clue.text: I work in the gallery to provide stimulation

indicators.note: I and the work go inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: An artist hoping that a job at the gallery will be exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and the work inside the gallery's name; the Tate is the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse pleasantly.

clue.text: On the other side in the Continental ball game

indicators.note: the other side goes inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
across means on the other side

explanation.surface: A sport played across the Channel in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the other side inside the French article. The answer is a team game played with netted sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport in which a ball is carried and thrown with netted sticks.

clue.text: Evangelist married after a struggle, showing little enthusiasm

indicators.note: the married letter comes after the struggle

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
a war is a struggle

explanation.surface: A preacher wed after a fight and is now half-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, literally tepid, describes a half-hearted, unenthusiastic attitude.

clue.text: Eulenspiegel's money-box?

explanation.surface: Asking whether the German folk prankster kept a cash box.
explanation.definitionFit: Till Eulenspiegel is the trickster of German folk tales, and a till is a cash drawer in a shop.

clue.text: The old salt in the ocean greyhound?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a veteran sailor is a racing dog at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is a veteran sailor; read literally it is a dog of the sea, a hound on the waves.

clue.text: Crew member who created Dracula

explanation.surface: A sailor who wrote the vampire novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker shovels coal into a ship's furnace; Bram Stoker wrote the novel about the vampire count.

clue.text: Haul in vessel, making king nervously irritable

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
being on edge means being nervously irritable

explanation.surface: A ship is pulled in, putting the monarch in a twitchy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: To kedge is to move a ship by hauling on a small anchor dropped ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedging moves a ship by winching it towards a small anchor carried ahead.

clue.text: Quarters outside Leeds, possibly superfluous

indicators.note: the compass quarters stand outside the rearranged city

parts.note: N, E and S are three of the four compass quarters

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of the city could be set out another way

explanation.surface: Neighbourhoods round a northern English city may be unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the city, giving EDLES, and 'outside' sets two quarters before it and one after. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless is unnecessary, more than required.

clue.text: Periods on the organ

explanation.surface: Breaks in playing at the church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Stops are full stops ending sentences, and organ stops are knobs selecting ranks of pipes.

clue.text: A plot put together in a place of retirement

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A garden patch combined with a spot for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests old age but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means tucked up in bed, where one retires at night.

clue.text: What a bloomer, making the game last too long

parts.note: snap is a children's card game
to drag on is to last too long

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a blunder that makes the game go on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant. Snap is a card game where players call out matching cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant that flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Southern see always controlled harshly

indicators.note: the first pieces hold, or control, the next word within them

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
ever means always

explanation.surface: A southern diocese is run strictly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled' puts always inside the southern see. A see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely means in a strict, stern or harsh way.

clue.text: Rock used, eg, in intricate craft

indicators.note: intricate means complex and tangled, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a craft

explanation.surface: Stone used, for instance, in a complicated piece of handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intricate' rearranges EG and IN into GNEI. Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse banded metamorphic stone.
